files.note: Changed between the releases: the binary and multipart calls no longer pass a retry field, since 8.0.0 derives the policy from the request's shape. Paths, validation and parsing are unchanged; the claim now names the derived policy instead of a declared one.

Changed between the releases: the multipart body builder moved out to src/upload-source.ts, now cited separately, and request() derives the retry policy from the request's shape instead of taking it from the call site. A multipart body is still sent without a JSON content type. The claim is rewritten for the new split.
New in 8.0.0: the multipart body builder moved here from src/client-core.ts, where it was cited at cc7751c. First cited at this review.
Changed between the releases: only the comment on MULTIPART_FIELD_NAME, which now says src/upload-source.ts both appends and looks up the field. The value is still attachment.

Changed between the releases: deriveRetryPolicy now selects the policy from the body kind, intent and response kind, a multipart body first, and getRetryPolicy survives only as a test oracle. The four policies themselves are unchanged. The claim now says how the policy is selected.
Changed between the releases: the version line, a Node 24 install requirement, and the --quiet, report-download, cache and retry notes. The --filename guidance cited here is unchanged.

Changed between the releases only in the shipped build: 9.0.0 no longer emits source maps, so dist/modules/attachments.js lost its trailing sourceMappingURL comment. The source is unchanged, so the claim stands.

Changed between the releases only in the shipped build: 9.0.0 no longer emits source maps, so dist/validation.js lost its trailing sourceMappingURL comment. The source is unchanged, so the claim stands.

Changed between the releases: request() now starts the attempt timer before the host guard's DNS lookup and races it, connects through a dispatcher pinned to the validated DNS answers when the guard runs (not with allowPrivateHosts), labels a timer the aggregate budget owns as its duration stop, normalizes a fetch rejection that is not an Error, watches a multipart upload's transport so an aborted upload closes its part cleanly, and sends a single-token User-Agent. The multipart hand-off to createUploadSource, the retry policy derived from the request's shape and the body sent without a JSON content type are unchanged.

Changed between the releases: only the stream cleanup, in ownUploadStreams and the cleanup closure createUploadSource returns, which now closes a part cleanly once the transport is confirmed aborted and errors it otherwise. The FormData field, filename, openAsBlob media type and single build() cited here are unchanged.
Changed between the releases: it gained TESTRAIL_USER_EMAIL_PATTERN, the user email shape rule, and DEFAULT_TRANSPORT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS. MULTIPART_FIELD_NAME is still attachment.

Changed between the releases only in the shipped build: 9.0.0 no longer emits source maps, so dist/retry-policy.js lost its trailing sourceMappingURL comment. The source is unchanged, so the claim stands.

Changed between the releases: resolveFile now opens its input with O_NONBLOCK, so a FIFO is refused without waiting for a writer. The --filename override and the stdin naming advice cited here are unchanged.

New in 9.0.0: skill/SKILL.md was split into a short body and reference files, and the attachment recipes, with the --filename guidance cited from skill/SKILL.md at 8.0.0, moved here. First cited at this review.

sources.supports: addAttachmentToResult validates the result ID, places it as the only path segment of add_attachment_to_result and posts the file through the shared multipart pipeline with the caller's filename as a multipart body, which the core never retries. It parses no schema, so TestRail's reply is returned as received.

validateId accepts any positive integer: it tests Number.isInteger and has no safe-integer bound, so the largest-safe-integer ceiling on these identifiers is this server's own. validateEntryId and validateAttachmentId test strings against one case-insensitive UUID expression anchored at both ends, so a traversal sequence, a surrounding space or a trailing line terminator is refused; validateAttachmentId otherwise accepts any positive integer, with the same missing bound.

request() hands a multipart body to createUploadSource and derives its retry policy from the request's shape with deriveRetryPolicy, which selects the none policy for any multipart body before considering anything else, so an upload re-sends nothing, not even a 429. The built form data is the request body, sent without a JSON content type.

createUploadSource appends the file to a FormData under the field name attachment (MULTIPART_FIELD_NAME) with the caller's filename, and opens a path input with openAsBlob as a blob whose media type is the one supplied, as given, or empty when none was; FormData lowercases it when it wraps the blob as a File. Its build() refuses a second call, because the first one hands the descriptor over and releases it when the body has been consumed.

NO_RETRY_POLICY, the none policy, retries no status and no network error. deriveRetryPolicy selects it for every multipart body, ahead of any other input, because an upload is not idempotent and TestRail documents no retry semantics for one, so zero retries is the safe default.
The filename flag overrides the basename-derived filename when a caller wants to rename on upload, and callers reading from stdin are encouraged to pass one so TestRail stores a sensible value.
The --filename option overrides the path basename so the attachment shows up with a meaningful name in the TestRail UI.

add_attachment_to_result/{result_id} requires TestRail 5.7 or later and works only when the ability to edit test results is enabled under Site Settings. The upload must be multipart/form-data, the maximum upload size is 256MB, and the reply is {"attachment_id": 443}. It answers 400 for a malformed request or an invalid result ID and 403 for no access or insufficient permissions.
The documented attachment upload posts the file as the multipart field attachment to add_attachment_to_result/1 and receives {"attachment_id":11}.

input_policy.notes: Strictness is an MCP boundary requirement. The transport requires the caller's file to lie within the configured upload roots, stages an owned copy of it in its own staging directory before dispatch and hands the driver that copy, so the bytes sent are the bytes approved; the containment, the staging, its size limit and its disposal belong to the transport rather than to this endpoint.

outer_result.notes: TestRail answers with the new attachment_id, returned as the driver received it: the upload methods parse no schema. Drift is checked, advisorily, against the driver's attachment schema with attachment_id required as a positive safe integer or UUID, matching the identifiers accepted by attachment reads and deletes. A missing or malformed ID produces a warning without changing the reply.

parameters.semantics: No coercion. The validated number is passed positionally and appears verbatim as its path segment.

wire.encoding: Decimal integer path segment; numeric strings are rejected rather than coerced.

parameters.semantics: The caller's path to the file. The transport requires it to lie within the configured upload roots, stages an owned copy in its own staging directory, and the driver receives that copy's path, so this value never reaches TestRail; the file's contents do.

wire.encoding: The file's contents become the attachment part's body.

requirements.description: Pass the staged copy's path as the file argument.
Accept a path and upload that file's contents.
Reject a path carrying a control character before driver invocation.
Reject a missing path.

parameters.semantics: The name sent as the attachment part's filename, independent of the file's own name. The driver's CLI source and skill document describe it as the name TestRail stores and shows for the attachment; TestRail's reference does not say how it uses it. A path separator, a drive prefix, a lone . or .., a control byte and a double quote are refused: the name is not a path, and the encoder percent-escapes a quote, so the part would carry a name the caller never asked for.

wire.encoding: Sent as the attachment part's filename.

requirements.description: Pass the name as the filename argument and send it as the part's filename.
Accept a plain file name and send it even though the file itself is named differently.
Reject a name containing a forward or back slash before driver invocation.
Reject a name containing a double quote, which the multipart encoder percent-escapes, so the recorded name would differ from the one requested.
Reject a name that is only . or .., which names a directory rather than a file.
Reject a name that starts with a drive letter and a colon.
Reject a name carrying a control character.
Reject a missing name.

parameters.semantics: The media type recorded for the part, as a type and subtype with optional parameters whose quoted values are printable ASCII. Omitting it leaves the part's type undeclared, which the encoder writes as application/octet-stream; a supplied value becomes the staged copy's type, which FormData lowercases when it wraps the blob as a File.

wire.encoding: Sent lowercased as the attachment part's content type. With none supplied the part carries application/octet-stream, which is what the encoder writes for a blob with no declared type.

requirements.description: Pass the value as the staged file's type.
Accept a media type and send it on the part.
Accept a media type with a parameter and send it on the part.
Accept an upper-case media type, which the part carries lowercased.
Reject a value that is not a media type before driver invocation, including a quoted parameter value outside printable ASCII.
Declare no type on the staged copy when the caller supplied none, leaving the encoder's application/octet-stream on the part.
